historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2025 against FY2022 (3yr) and FY2020 (5yr). Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - cash taxes on net-share settlement (FY2024 218.3, FY2025 81.1) - interest income, applied to every year. Owner-FCF and EPS CAGRs are not meaningful: both start points are negative (owner FCF -401 in FY2022 and -1,584 in FY2020; EPS -0.18 and -1.20). Reported FCF compounded 125%/yr over three years while owner FCF only turned durably positive in FY2025 -- until then SBC consumed more than the whole reported free cash flow (FY2024: reported 1,141, owner 35). Equity CAGR (37.5%) is within 30% of revenue CAGR (32.6%) so no divergence flag, but note equity growth is itself partly SBC credited to paid-in capital. The selected 37.5% is NOT used as the forward path: current growth (Q3-2026 revenue +96% YoY) is far above it and the scenario paths decelerate from the live run-rate through it to a 3% terminal rate.

scenario_narratives.base: AIP keeps converting US commercial pilots and bootcamps into enterprise-wide deployments and US government demand (defence, intelligence, civil) stays strong, but the growth rate halves each year or two as the base gets large: US commercial (TTM growth >100%, now the largest single line at ~$984m a quarter) decelerates as the first wave of large accounts saturates, and government growth settles toward budget-linked rates. Revenue reaches ~$44bn in year 10 -- roughly Salesforce's size today. The 62% adjusted operating margin is treated as a peak produced by revenue outrunning hiring; it fades to 52% as headcount, go-to-market spend and hyperscaler/LLM pass-through costs catch up and as larger, lower-margin government programmes grow in the mix. SBC drifts from 13.5% to 9% of revenue at the house default of 0.5pp a year. Cash tax rises from ~3% to 21% by year 5 as the $9bn federal NOL and the excess-deduction windfall are used up.
scenario_narratives.bull: Palantir becomes the default enterprise AI operating layer: the ontology proves to be a durable moat against both hyperscaler-native agent platforms and the model labs moving up-stack, US commercial keeps compounding above 50% for several more years, international commercial (currently stagnant, 19% of revenue) re-accelerates, and defence modernisation programmes scale into multi-billion-dollar annual lines. Revenue passes $77bn in year 10 and operating leverage is largely retained (58% mature EBITDA margin before SBC) because the product is deployed with few forward-deployed engineers per dollar of revenue. SBC falls to 8% as the share price does the work of retention. This case needs every one of those things -- moat, international, government scale and margin retention -- to hold at once.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025-26 surge turns out to be a deployment wave rather than a new growth rate. Three axes: (1) US government, ~41% of revenue through contracts terminable for convenience, flattens under budget pressure, a change of administration priorities or procurement backlash against concentration in one vendor; (2) US commercial AIP spend proves partly experimental -- enterprises standardise on cheaper hyperscaler or model-lab agent tooling and top-20 customer revenue (now $146m each, +76%) stops expanding; (3) remaining performance obligations of only $4.9bn against $7.3bn of TTM revenue mean there is little contractual cushion when bookings slow. Growth drops to the teens within two years, margins revert to 42% as pricing tightens and the company keeps hiring, and SBC stays above 12% of revenue because a falling share price forces larger grants. The business remains very profitable and cash-rich -- no terminal floor is hit -- but it is a ~$20bn-revenue company in year 10, not a $40bn+ one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Palantir is an exceptional business at the moment -- revenue nearly doubling year on year with a 62% adjusted operating margin, no debt and $10.6bn of net cash -- and the model gives it credit for that: the base case compounds revenue 6.0x in a decade at a mature margin that only a handful of software companies have ever sustained, and the bull case 10x. What the model refuses to do is capitalise peak hypergrowth or a peak margin in perpetuity: growth decelerates every year to a 3% terminal rate, the margin fades from its high, SBC (13.5% of revenue, and not offset by buybacks) is charged in full, interest on the cash pile is stripped because the cash is added separately, and the near-zero cash tax rate is ramped to 21% as the NOL shield runs out. On that basis even the bull case sits well below the market price: the price is paying for an outcome beyond the bull path, sustained for longer, or discounted at a far lower rate than 10%. The required-return table shows what return today's price implies on the base path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Upside risk to the model: sequential growth has accelerated for three straight quarters (+16%, +18.5%, +19.5% QoQ); if that persists through 2027 the base year-1 and year-2 growth rates are too low and every later year compounds off a higher base
Terminal dependence: most of enterprise value sits in the terminal year, which rests on a year-10 margin and revenue level that cannot be observed today
US government concentration (~41% of revenue) on contracts terminable for convenience; RPO of $4.9bn is less than eight months of TTM revenue
Margin durability: the 60%+ adjusted margin has existed for three quarters; the base case assumes 52% at maturity, the bear 42%

SBC and dilution: SBC is ~$1.3bn annualised and rising with the share price (new RSUs granted at ~$131 vs a $28 legacy average); 146.8m very low-strike options remain outstanding; buybacks are negligible
Cash tax timing: the $9bn federal NOL and excess stock-deduction windfall could shelter income longer than the 5-year ramp assumes (upside) or be limited under Section 382 or law changes (downside)
Year 1 is a TTM-forward year, not a fiscal year: only its first quarter (Q4-2026) is covered by guidance; the other three quarters are a judged sequential path

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 106.37-212.94
data_sources.financials: PLTR_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (SEC XBRL) for the history; Q3-2026 10-Q (PLTR_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, cash flow, SBC and employer-payroll-tax reconciliation, award tables and share counts; FY2025 10-K (PLTR_Annual_FY2025.txt) for NOLs, full-year SBC, equity-award taxes and buybacks
data_sources.qualitative: PLTR_Analysis.json for the raised FY2026 guidance; segment, customer, RPO, remaining-deal-value and risk-factor disclosures in the FY2025 10-K and Q3-2026 10-Q

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-09-30, treasury-stock method at the current price: 2,409.2m Class A/B/F shares outstanding + 146.8m options (weighted strike $10.16, ~137.9m net) + 35.5m unvested RSUs + 0.14m P-RSUs + ~3.6m net from 18.5m SARs (strike $134.77). Q3-2026 diluted weighted average was 2,573.9m; the period-end figure is used because it is later and larger. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-09-30 = FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back 684.0 less 9M-2025 487.6 plus 9M-2026 785.7 (Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement). Cash taxes on net-share settlement were nil in the TTM window (FY2025's 81.1 all fell in H1-2025; 9M-2026 'other financing activities' is only -2.5), so nothing is added. Employer payroll taxes on SBC (95.0 TTM) are a cash operating cost already inside reported OCF; they are NOT added to SBC here and are instead charged inside the EBITDA margin path (which is adjusted operating margin + D&A - employer payroll taxes).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.5% (10-year UST; the Q3-2026 10-Q itself uses 4.9% for long-dated SAR grants), equity risk premium ~4.75%, beta 1.15 (below the raw trailing beta, which is inflated by the stock's retail-driven volatility; contract revenue is sticky and the balance sheet is all-equity with $10.6bn net cash) -> ~10.0%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. The same 10% is used in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: the lease cost is an operating expense inside EBITDA, so it is already in the flows. Operating lease liabilities (~$0.28bn) are NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore omitted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial (book $117.1m; ~$6m of quarterly net income, <1%). Flows are consolidated and NCI is deducted once, at book, in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, three scenarios, probability-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 1: operating software company; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/shell, no live corporate action). First valuation of this ticker -- fresh build, no reconciliation. BASE PERIOD: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30, not FY2025, because FY2025 revenue (4,475) is already 39% below the TTM (7,288) and 52% below the Q3-2026 annualised run-rate (9,254); year 1 is therefore the 12 months to 2027-09-30 and the balance sheet date matches the start of the flows. OWNER FCF: TTM reported FCF 4,054.0 (OCF 4,097.2 less capex 43.2) - SBC 982.1 - interest income 295.6 = 2,776.3 (38.1% of revenue). Interest income is stripped because net cash (10.6bn) is 3.8x the owner-FCF base; leaving it in would count the cash pile twice. BUYBACKS: PLTR is effectively a non-repurchaser (TTM ~$21m against $982m of SBC) -- the flat share count is a modelling convention the company is not funding with cash; basic shares rose ~0.75% in 9M-2026 and SBC is the charge for that. NET CASH: cash and equivalents 3,619.4 + marketable securities 6,942.1 (6,756.7 US Treasuries/AFS debt + ~185 listed equities); no debt, $500m revolver undrawn. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-10%). Receivables (1,883) plus prepaids (323) exceed contract liabilities (1,207) plus payables (624), and in 9M-2026 working capital consumed ~$432m against a ~$2.8bn YoY revenue increase; growth consumes cash here despite customer deposits. CASH TAX: FY2026 provision is ~1.3% of pre-tax income; US federal NOLs were $9.0bn at FY2025 ($8.3bn indefinite) and are still growing because RSUs granted near $28 vest at 5x that, producing tax deductions far above the book SBC expense. The shield is real but finite -- the path ramps to 21% by year 5 and the terminal year carries the full rate. GUIDANCE: FY2026 revenue guidance was raised with Q3 to $8,530-8,534m (~+91% YoY; per PLTR_Analysis.json -- the figure is in the earnings release, not the 10-Q), implying Q4-2026 of ~2,650 (+14.6% QoQ) against 9M actuals of 5,881.5. Year 1 (the 12 months to 2027-09-30) takes that Q4 as its first quarter in the base and bear cases; the last three quarters grew +16%, +18.5%, +19.5% QoQ. The adjusted-FCF guide of $4.8-5.0bn is on the company basis (before SBC, including interest income, adding back employer payroll tax) and is not the owner-FCF base. Scenario axes are drawn from the 10-K/10-Q segment, RPO, customer and risk-factor disclosures; PLTR_Analysis.json landed while this build was in progress and was used for the guidance figure only. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: Revenue -> ~20.5bn in ten years (2.8x): year 1 at +48% is Q4-2026 at guidance and then near-flat quarters (+2-3% QoQ), after which growth collapses to the high teens and single digits. Margin mean-reverts to 42% and SBC stays near 12-13% because comp is sticky when the share price falls.

base.narrative: Revenue 7.3bn -> ~43.9bn in ten years (6.0x). Year 1 at +65% is Q4-2026 at the guided ~2,650 followed by sequential growth of 9%, 8% and 7% -- under half the recent ~19% QoQ pace. EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, after employer payroll tax) fades from the current ~60% to 52%, a level only the best mature software franchises hold. Terminal owner-FCF margin ~33%.

bull.narrative: Revenue -> ~77.5bn in ten years (10.6x); year 1 at +80% is a Q4-2026 beat (~2,750) then 13%/12%/11% sequential growth, with today's 62% adjusted margin essentially held (58% at maturity) and SBC falling to 8% of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): about 41% of revenue comes from one customer class, the US government, on terminable-for-convenience contracts, and RPO covers well under a year of revenue -- but there is no solvency or refinancing risk with $10.6bn net cash, so it is not raised further. Base 50%: it already assumes a 6.0x revenue increase at best-in-class margins. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs the moat, international re-acceleration, government scale-up and margin retention to all hold simultaneously, although current momentum (sequential growth accelerating for three straight quarters) keeps it well above a tail probability.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
